plain: To give up land or power to another country or ruler, usually by treaty.

webster.text: To yield; to surrender; to give up; to resign; as, to cede a fortress, a province or country, by treaty.

example.quote: It is true, the states, when they shall cede places, may stipulate, that the laws and government of congress in them, shall always be formed on such principles; but it is easy to discern, that the stipulations of a state, or of the inhabitants of the place ceded, can be of but little avail against the power and gradual encroachments of the union.
example.cite: Letters from the Federal Farmer to the Republican, Letter XVIII, Jan. 25, 1788
